scores.evidence: Integer minor units plus ISO 4217 currency, no floats. Append-only double-entry ledger: a DB trigger rejects UPDATE/DELETE.
scores.rationale: Claims about Stripe Connect Standard, SAQ A via hosted fields, RLS without BYPASSRLS, gapless numbering via per-tenant row lock, and transactional outbox are all accurate, including the subtle areas.

scores.evidence: I read the request as: the billing platform is the product. Tenant businesses use it to bill their own end customers.
scores.rationale: Ambiguity is resolved explicitly with alternatives mapped to plan changes and scope is credibly buildable, but price versioning (grandfathered prices), trials and pauses — implied core billing capabilities — are not specified.

scores.evidence: Ledger, invoices and payments are consistent first... Usage ingest is available first: accept to a durable log, dedupe by idempotency key, rate later
scores.rationale: Component responsibilities, data ownership, consistency choices and the home_cell seam are stated once and honored consistently across phases with no contradictions.

scores.evidence: 0 invariant violations... over ≥ 1M generated sequences. 100% match on ≥ 150 golden cases. Finance lead signs off
scores.rationale: Twelve validations with hypotheses, methods, thresholds, evidence and failure branches; the riskiest assumptions (money model, isolation, double-charge) gate early phases, and daily reconciliation continues in production.

scores.evidence: ASSUMPTION: tenants call it inside their own signup and checkout flows... UNKNOWN: needs projected tenants × peak events/s from the product owner
scores.rationale: Every number carries an ASSUMPTION or UNKNOWN label with an owner and deadline, and the plan states exactly how the design changes if the main assumptions are wrong.

scores.evidence: Chaos test in Stripe test mode: provider timeouts, worker killed between the Stripe call and commit, duplicated and reordered webhooks
scores.rationale: Covers the hard domain failures — double charges, charge-status-unknown, out-of-order webhooks, tax outage holding finalization, cross-tenant leaks, noisy neighbors, corruption via hourly ledger-balance checks — with concrete detection and recovery.

scores.evidence: Alerts fire on 5xx rate, outbox lag, webhook signature failures and a ledger-balance check that runs hourly.
scores.rationale: Blue/green deploys, expand/contract migrations, domain-meaningful alerts, kill switches, runbooks, SLO burn-rate alerts and an explicit complexity budget sized to one team of 8.

scores.evidence: Per-invoice cost (tax API, payment-provider platform fees, infrastructure, email) leaves margin at our price
scores.rationale: The dominant cost drivers, controls (cache/batch tax calls, renegotiate) and the build-vs-buy trade-off are covered, but there is no order-of-magnitude build or run estimate before beta measurement.

scores.evidence: R3: tenant ID in every row and key, and data cannot be split cleanly later
scores.rationale: Each decision is classified by reversibility with revisit triggers, hard-to-reverse choices (tenancy, money model, IDs, fund flow) are validated earliest, seams like home_cell and TaxProvider provide explicit exit paths, and the point of no return is flagged.

scores.evidence: 2 deployables (core, ingest) plus managed Postgres, a managed queue and the payment and tax vendors; no self-hosted Kafka
scores.rationale: Enforces a complexity budget, defers columnar store, multi-region, rev-rec and e-invoicing with explicit pull-forward triggers, while omitting no billing essentials.

scores.evidence: Exit check (V0): The request above succeeds with one trace across every tier. One deploy and one rollback both succeed
scores.rationale: Phases are ordered by rework-width with task lists, dependency-justified gates, checkable exit criteria, and explicit fallback actions when any validation fails; a team could start on Phase 0 immediately.

checklist.evidence: Integer minor units plus ISO 4217 currency, no floats... Documented rounding per line
a DB trigger rejects UPDATE/DELETE. Finalized invoices are immutable; corrections go through credit notes
idempotency key derived from (invoice, attempt number)... Webhook ingestion with dedupe and out-of-order handling
No card numbers ever: only the provider's hosted fields and tokens... a state machine that tolerates "charge status unknown"
Row-level security (RLS) enforced by an app role without `BYPASSRLS`... tenant A's credentials try B's IDs on every route
with 5% duplicates and out-of-order events injected... 0 lost and 0 double-counted events... Usage invoice lines that link to their aggregates
Subscription lifecycle with upgrades, downgrades and proration... Periods stored in UTC, anchored in the tenant's timezone
Tax-ID capture and validation (VIES for EU)... Gapless per-tenant invoice numbers, assigned at finalization... Retention policy enforcement
Dunning schedules, refunds and disputes... Stripe-hosted payment-method updates... dunning backoff
Daily reconciliation of the ledger against Stripe balance transactions, alerting on any difference
Ingest must keep accepting events while the core is down
Build the billing core (it is the product). Buy the payment provider (Stripe Connect), tax engine (Stripe Tax or Avalara...)

traps.evidence: Integer minor units plus ISO 4217 currency, no floats
Finalized invoices are immutable; corrections go through credit notes
`Idempotency-Key` required on every POST... webhook receiver (signature verified)... dedupe and out-of-order handling
No card numbers ever: only the provider's hosted fields and tokens... PCI scope confirmed as SAQ A
a CI lint that fails any table without `tenant_id`, `mode` and RLS... V2 re-run in CI covers every new route

note: An exemplary, near-reference-quality plan — correct on the hard billing mechanics, with disciplined assumptions and validation gates; only notable gaps are price versioning/trials in the subscription lifecycle and pre-beta cost estimates.
